# Cut Contour Templates: PDFs for Onyx and a Graphtec Cutter

A **Cut Contour template** turns each photo or PDF of a product into a PDF that's ready for Onyx RIP and a Graphtec cutter. You set the finished size and the bleed once, and OrderHub Desktop does the rest for every job of that product.

Each PDF it makes has:

* a page that is the finished size plus the bleed on every side;
* the artwork filling the whole page, bleed included;
* a rectangle cut line exactly round the finished size, in a spot colour named **CutContour**. It's set to overprint, sits on its own layer called **Cut Contour**, and is drawn on top of everything else.

---

## Before you start

Cut Contour templates only work on a **PDF Copy** or **Folder Copy** controller with **Apply Prepress templates** ticked:

1. Go to **Settings → Routing → Order Controllers** and click **Edit** on the PDF Copy or Folder Copy controller that sends to Onyx.
2. Tick **Apply Prepress templates (Settings → Prepress)**.
3. Click **Save**.

* Note: Any other controller, such as Darkroom Pro, Epson or Fuji, ignores Cut Contour templates.

---

## Adding a Cut Contour template

1. Go to **Settings → Prepress → Cut Contour Templates**.
2. Click **+ Add Template**.
3. In **Name**, enter something that tells you which product it is, for example `Canvas 100×150`.
4. In **Unit**, pick **in** or **mm**. A new template starts in inches.
   * Note: Switching the unit just shows the same sizes in the other unit. It never changes what is cut.
5. Enter the **Finished width** and **Finished height**: the size after cutting.
6. In **Bleed**, enter the extra artwork round each edge, which the cutter cuts off. A new template starts at 0.125 in.
   * Note: 0 is allowed, but then the cut line sits on the page edge. Save warns you about this.
7. Leave **Cut line width (pt)** at 0.25 unless your cutter needs otherwise. It can be 0.25 to 0.5 pt.
8. Under **Product Codes**, click **+ Add Product Code** and enter each product code this template handles.
   * Note: A product code can belong to only one Prepress template. If it's already used, Save tells you which template has it.
9. Optional: in **Output Path**, click **Browse...** and choose Onyx's hot folder. Leave it blank to use the controller's output path.
10. Make sure **Enabled** is ticked, then click **Save Template**.

Under the sizes, the window spells out the result, for example "Page 8.25 × 10.25 in · cut line at 8 × 10 in".

![Edit Cut Contour Window](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/f6402059-3cfd-48db-a0d4-9cf71bd6f0dc.png)

To stop using a template without deleting it, untick **Enabled**.

---

## What lands in the folder

Each photo or PDF in the job becomes one PDF, directly in the output folder (no sub-folders):

* `{order number}_{job id}_{file name}_QTY{copies}.pdf`
* Reprints end `_R1`, `_R2` and so on.

**Nothing is ever overwritten.** If a file with the same name is already there, the new one gets **_2**, **_3** and so on.

The banner sheet and PDF steps from the controller are **not** added, because an extra page or stamp would be printed and cut.

Once the PDFs are written, the job is marked In Production. Complete it in OrderHub once it's printed and cut.

---

## How the artwork is placed

| Artwork | What happens |
|---|---|
| JPEG, PNG or TIFF | Scaled to cover the whole page and centred. Nothing is stretched, so if the photo's shape differs from the page, its edges are trimmed off. |
| PDF with its own trim box | Placed so its trim lines up with the cut line. |
| PDF exactly the finished size (no bleed) | Enlarged just enough to fill the bleed. The Activity Log says by how much. |
| Any other PDF | Scaled to cover the page and centred. |

* **Multi-page PDFs:** every page gets its own page and cut line.
* **Phone photos come out upright.** A photo stored sideways (as phones do) is turned upright first.
* **One template covers both orientations.** A portrait photo on a landscape template, or the other way round, gets the template turned for that file. So a 150 × 100 mm template also handles 100 × 150 mm photos.

---

## When a job isn't sent

If any file in the job can't be used, **nothing** from the job is written, and the job shows why:

| Message starts | What to do |
|---|---|
| "…is a CMYK JPEG…" (or CMYK TIFF) | Save the file as RGB and send it again. |
| "…already has a CutContour cut line." | The PDF has its own cut line, so two would be cut. Remove it, or send the job without the template. |
| "…is rotated, which cut contour templates can't place yet." | Save the PDF with the page upright. |
| "…has no PDF, JPEG, PNG or TIFF files…" | Convert the files to one of those types. |
| "…could not be made into a cut contour PDF…" | The file is damaged. Ask for the order to be sent again. |

A refused reprint shows the message in the Reprint window and leaves the original job alone.

---

## Good to know

* **Check your first job.** Make sure Onyx picks up **CutContour** as the cut path and doesn't print it, and that the Graphtec cuts on the finished size with the bleed falling outside.
* **The Activity Log shows each send**, for example "Cut contour PDF written — PXDEMO-ABC123 → 2 files, 100 × 150 mm, 3 mm bleed".
* **Sizes stay exactly as you enter them.** Opening and saving a template, or switching its unit, never changes the size it cuts.
